main_topics.reason: The user described renewed urgency and visible blood, said the symptoms were gradually worsening, and returned to whether this could signal a flare.
The user repeatedly asked whether Humira could stop working because of antibodies, how that happens, and how clinicians might test for it.
The user asked whether it was reasonable to wait several weeks for the gastro appointment despite the blood and worsening symptoms.
The user asked whether a failing Humira would lead to a dose change or a switch and whether other options existed.
The user asked what foods might help during urgency and said they almost did not want to eat when symptoms were bad.
The user said they were scared the worsening symptoms were the start of a flare and that they had been spiralling.

output.summary: After months of stability on Humira, the user reported several days of renewed urgency and small amounts of blood that were getting worse, and asked about antibodies, testing, and treatment options. They also asked whether they could wait for a gastro appointment in a few weeks; the assistant largely supported waiting unless things changed dramatically, despite the reported worsening, and the user ended feeling calmer with a list of questions for the visit.
